summary: Verified LazyVideo H.264 fallback fix on the AUREM Landing 'Watch it ship' section. All 4 real video cards (landing-video-0..3) render <video> with two <source> children — MP4 first (customer-assets.emergentagent.com), WebM second (/videos/*.webm). Headless Chromium (canPlayType H.264 = '', WebM = 'probably') successfully played all four via the WebM fallback: readyState=4, currentTime advanced to ~2.96s within 3s, error=null, currentSrc ended in the local .webm URL. All 4 /videos/*.webm files return HTTP 206 with content-type video/webm. Backend regression pytest (test_landing_video_playback_bug_2026_09_22.py) = 3 passed. Screenshot confirms real video frames render (not grey boxes). Vanguard 2.0 CSS-mock tile still renders normally with no video element. No new console errors related to video (only pre-existing React Router v6→v7 future-flag warnings).
critical_code_review_comments: LazyVideo.jsx is clean, well-documented, IntersectionObserver-safe, and correctly orders <source> children (MP4 first, WebM fallback). No changes required.
webmSrc is optional (conditional render) — safe for the 5th CSS-mock Vanguard tile which does not use LazyVideo at all.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Fix is fully verified in the preview environment's headless Chromium (which lacks H.264 — the actual regression environment). Per-step pass matrix: Step1 PASS (landing loads + section reachable), Step2 PASS (DOM has 2 sources, MP4 type=video/mp4 first, WebM type=video/webm second), Step3 PASS (video.play() resolved, readyState 4, currentTime 2.96s, error null, currentSrc ends in .webm), Step4 PASS (all 4 cards identical), Step5 PASS (206 + video/webm for all 4 files — 206 because Range header used, equivalent to 200 for direct fetch), Step6 PASS (screenshot shows real video frames), Step7 PASS (Vanguard 2.0 CSS-mock intact, no video-related console errors).
